- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, overestimate the peak and underreact to subsequent volatility.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model tends to overshoot and continue upward — correct by introducing a downward bias after day 3–5 of the spike.  
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model underestimates the price rise — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% of recent 7-day average.  
- If supply net is positive and sentiment is bearish, model overestimates the decline — apply a ceiling to forecast at 10–15% below recent high.  
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model fails to adjust — apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overreacting to sentiment shifts.  
- For 30-day forecasts, mean reversion is strong in high-volatility periods — cap forecast at ±15% of 30-day moving average unless driven by strong policy or auction events.  
- If recent auction supply is high (e.g., CAP3 EU/DE), model underestimates price drop — add 1–3% downward adjustment to forecast.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to drift toward recent mean — avoid overfitting to recent trend; use 30-day median as anchor.
